```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
```

`nm_wasserstein()` implements the method of Simon, Hulot and von Fabeck
(Front Pharmacol 2026, doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1804989). For one or several
runs, it compares the distribution of the individual deviations (ETA)
between groups of subjects defined by a covariate:

* the distance between the two distributions is the 1-Wasserstein distance
  W (the area between their empirical cumulative distributions); its p-value
  comes from a permutation test, and a t-test is given for reference;
* a categorical covariate compares its levels; a continuous covariate
  compares its 4th and 1st quartiles (`continuous = "extremes"`, default) or
  every pair of quartiles (`continuous = "pairwise"`, Bonferroni-adjusted);
* a Wasserstein-based R2, `R2W = 1 - W/W_ref`, where W is the distance of the
  ETA distribution to 0, measures how much of the variability left in the
  reference run is explained by a model; the ETA shrinkage is reported with
  it.

## Example

The example project of the package contains a BASE model without covariate
and a FINAL model with body weight and genotype on CL (simulated data, see
`vignette("nmpilot")`). The covariates are read from the data set named in
`$DATA`; the ETA on CL is found from the model code.

```{r w}
library(nmpilot)
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "nmpilot")
w <- nm_wasserstein(
  runs       = c(BASE = file.path(ex, "run1.reg"), FINAL = file.path(ex, "run2.reg")),
  covariates = c("WT", "GENO"),
  eta        = "CL",
  n_perm     = 2000
)
w
```

In the BASE model the distribution of the CL deviations differs strongly
between genotypes; in the FINAL model, where genotype is in the model, the two
distributions overlap.

```{r ecdf}
plot(w)
```

```{r r2w, fig.height = 3.5}
plot(w, type = "r2w")
```

## Several pairs of quartiles

```{r pairwise}
wp <- nm_wasserstein(c(BASE = file.path(ex, "run1.reg")), covariates = "WT",
                     eta = "CL", n_perm = 2000, continuous = "pairwise")
wp$tests[, c("comparison", "W", "p_W", "p_W_adj")]
```

## Inputs

`runs` takes run directories of any name (`run1.reg`, `run1.nm7`, `run1/`) or
a run prefix (`"C:/study/run1"` for `run1.ext`, `run1.phi` and `run1.ctl` in
the same folder). Each run needs its `.phi` (individual ETAs), `.ext`
(OMEGA, for the shrinkage) and control stream. The covariates can also be
given directly with `data`, a data.frame or a CSV file with one row per
subject.
